field_edits.updated_text: Scapholunate ligament shows abnormal morphology compatible with chronic insufficiency/tear, with widening of the scapholunate interval.
Degenerative changes are present involving the lunotriquetral articulation.
Flexor tendons are grossly intact. Mild fluid/synovial prominence surrounds the flexor tendons at the carpal tunnel.
Visualized extensor tendons are grossly intact without definite high-grade tear.
Median nerve demonstrates mild increased signal and flattening within the carpal tunnel, compatible with median neuropathy/carpal tunnel syndrome. No discrete compressive mass identified.
No acute fracture or focal aggressive osseous lesion. Advanced multifocal degenerative changes involving the carpal bones with subchondral sclerosis, cystic change, and marrow edema-like signal.
Marked joint space narrowing with small associated joint effusions and synovial hypertrophic/degenerative changes. No subluxation. The radiocarpal and intercarpal articulations are maintained.
Degenerative thinning and irregularity of the triangular fibrocartilage complex. No definite acute full-thickness tear identified.
Mild diffuse soft-tissue edema about the wrist.

impression:
1. Advanced multifocal degenerative osteoarthritis of the left wrist with marked joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, cystic change, osteophyte formation, and extensive cartilage loss.
2. Chronic scapholunate ligament insufficiency/tear with widening of the scapholunate interval.
3. Degenerative changes of the lunotriquetral articulation.
4. Degenerative thinning and irregularity of the triangular fibrocartilage complex without acute full-thickness tear.
5. Mild median neuropathy/carpal tunnel syndrome evidenced by flattening and increased signal of the median nerve.
6. Small joint effusions with synovial hypertrophy.
7. Mild diffuse soft-tissue edema about the wrist.
